approach.method_basis: The Parent is a graph genetic optimizer with two proposal sources and a Bayesian gatekeeper. It keeps the 64 best molecules it has actually had scored, draws breeding parents from the top score quantiles, and builds a surplus field of 160 fresh candidates for every announced batch of ten. Three quarters of that field come from the inherited graph generator: roughly two attempts in five recombine a connected fragment of two parents, the rest apply one to three successive single-atom or single-bond edits to one parent, with a longer walk when the local neighbourhood keeps rejecting. The remaining quarter - every fourth admitted slot - is written by a small autoregressive SMILES model trained during preparation on the supplied unlabeled corpus alone and then frozen and objective-blind: it takes the same score-quantile parent, cuts its serialization in half and writes a new ending, so one proposal can rebuild a ring system and several atoms at once. Every candidate from either source passes the same stable canonical identity check, two duplicate scopes and a narrow sulfur-admission gate. Which ten of the 160 are actually evaluated is decided by a Gaussian process fitted only to this session's accepted scores, on integer-count Morgan fingerprints under a generalized Tanimoto covariance; ten correlated draws from its joint posterior pick ten distinct candidates in sequence, each from the members not yet chosen, and accepted scores feed straight back into the archive and the greedy population. Because that surrogate knows only the neighbourhood of molecules it has already seen scored, it reliably prefers the near-copies of the incumbent over the distant chemistry the prior supplies.
approach.novelty: Reserve evaluations by proposal family instead of letting one price list arbitrate both families. The supply stays exactly as it is; the only change is in the allocator's sequential choice. The first eight of the ten picks in every announced batch are taken exactly as before. For the last two picks the list of still-available candidates is narrowed to the prior-origin members not yet chosen, and the same posterior draw that was already made for those two positions picks its best candidate from that narrowed list. Two of ten evaluations per batch therefore go to the kind of candidate the surrogate has been declining, while eight remain its own free choice, and the chemistry, the model, the kernel, the normalization, the random numbers and the pool target are all untouched. This is the first arm on this lineage that pays for a proposal family rather than ranking it. The earlier allocation children all changed the field or the eligibility by model score - a fourfold wider field, a narrower field, the forty highest posterior means made eligible during a stall, or how long that stall lasted - and all of them left the surrogate free to spend every evaluation on whatever it priced highest; the round-42 arm changed what was on offer and was refused. It is also not another version of that refused recipe: the prior's share of the pool, its prefix rule, temperature, architecture and checkpoint are all held fixed, so a failure here closes the pricing question rather than inviting a sweep.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent's binding behaviour is not what it can propose but what its allocator will pay for. n-d527b3b4e2cb changed the proposal supply exactly as registered - a frozen corpus prior filled 17,302 of 69,600 admitted pool slots (realized share 0.2486, every session at or above 0.231) with chemistry far from its conditioning parent (median count-Morgan Tanimoto 0.6092 against 0.8326 for the graph arm, Murcko core changed 97.2% against 69.8%) - and the inherited accepted-only count-Morgan Tanimoto Gaussian process then bought that quarter of the supply with 231 of 4,350 evaluations (5.31%). 292 of the 435 announced batches bought none at all, all 29 batches of sitagliptin_mpo seed 2 bought none while taking 88 of the node's 98 slot fallbacks, the prior-origin group was priced below the graph-edit group in 433 of 435 batches, and the gap hardened within each session (0.0257 / 0.1155 / 0.1498 across session thirds) as cheap prior evaluations entered the accepted archive the kernel is fitted to. The few purchases that happened were uncertainty draws, not value draws (in-pool percentiles 0.780 uncertainty against 0.415 predicted score, while graph picks sat at 0.264 and 0.931). The panel fell 0.051941 against the Anchor and the prior-origin path returned 0.1405 of the node's 5.0403 realized incumbent-increment mass. The same refusal recurs on an unrelated supply intervention (n-36afb69ebdd1: 1.072% against 1.738% of picks per pooled candidate in a 640-member field), and the identical selector-eligibility interface has already been moved on this ancestry (n-61b9b3bfb40d). What no arm has ever done is make the allocator spend evaluations on candidates away from its own accepted archive, so the campaign cannot say whether that 5.31% destroyed a real gain or correctly protected a 300-evaluation budget.

adoptions.applicability: This Parent already has the paper's other two elements - a corpus-pretrained autoregressive SMILES generator and graph crossover/mutation offspring entering one scored candidate set over a rank-selected population of 64 - and round 42 measured that its one remaining difference, letting a single archive-fitted acquisition price both origins, spends 5.31% of the budget on 24.86% of the supply. The reserved-count pattern is therefore adopted alone, as a two-of-ten reservation inside the validated allocator, so the result attaches to the pricing question rather than to any policy-training claim; it transfers no reported benchmark number, which were measured at 10,000 oracle calls under AUC Top-10.
adoptions.borrowed_element: A fixed per-round integer split of the oracle budget between the two proposal origins - a reserved number of evaluations for learned-generator candidates, the remainder for graph crossover/mutation offspring - instead of ranking both origins against each other under a single acquisition score.

deviations.adopted_setting: Exactly two of the ten evaluations per announced batch, 20% of the budget, and the reserved picks are still chosen by the inherited correlated Thompson draw inside the restricted mask rather than sent to the oracle unfiltered.
deviations.paper_setting: The policy sample of each outer iteration is sent to the oracle directly, with numGen genetic generations scored alongside it; the per-round split is set by numGen (ablation indicates two generations and offspring size eight), so roughly a third of the calls go to policy samples.
deviations.reason: The protocol fixes the announced batch at ten and the budget at 300 accepted observations per task, a thirtieth of the paper's; and the arm's whole purpose is to hold the validated allocator fixed and change only which candidates it may buy, so the reservation must be the smallest integer that guarantees a purchase in every batch while leaving the surrogate the majority of the budget. One integer is bound before evaluation and no sweep follows.

deviations.adopted_setting: The prior stays frozen and objective-blind for the whole session with zero gradient updates, exactly as inherited; the reserved evaluations serve only the search.
deviations.paper_setting: The learned policy is updated online every round with a trajectory-balance loss, a KL penalty to the pretrained prior and rank-weighted replay, so the reserved calls also serve policy training.
deviations.reason: The supply must be held byte-identical for the allocation to be the single variable, and the campaign's registered conditions for this route forbid changing the prior recipe; an online update would also confound the pricing question with policy adaptation at 300 evaluations.

deviations.adopted_setting: The Parent's greedy-64 population, score-quantile parent sampling and 160-candidate pool are untouched, and no extra oracle call exists.
deviations.paper_setting: A population seeded from the scored buffer with its own genetic loop and its own oracle calls per generation.
deviations.reason: The per-node oracle budget, pool width, batch size and retention law are frozen by the stage profile and by this route's conditions.

adoptions.implementation_change: In FingerprintPosterior.select, the last two of the ten sequential picks per announced batch take their argmax of the same sampled posterior function inside an availability mask intersected with the not-yet-selected pool members whose origin tag is prior_continuation; the first eight picks and the entire draw, model and kernel are unchanged.

literature_review.conclusion: Adopt one element and only one: the fixed per-round integer reservation of oracle evaluations for the learned-generator origin, rather than letting a single acquisition score arbitrate both origins. Adapt it to this profile as two of the ten announced picks, still taken by the inherited correlated Thompson draw inside a mask restricted to unselected prior-origin members, with the prior, its share, prefix rule, temperature, architecture and checkpoint frozen and no online policy update, no extra oracle call and no change to pool width, population or retention. Reject the trajectory-balance update, the KL penalty, rank-weighted replay, direct oracle scoring of generator samples and every reported benchmark number, which are measured at 10,000 oracle calls under a different metric and are not campaign evidence. The conditions fit because the element adopted is precisely the one this Parent lacks - the allocator pays for a proposal family instead of pricing it - and because the campaign's own receipts fix the value, the interface and the predicted activation ranges, so a failure closes the pricing branch with receipts instead of authorizing a quota sweep.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The reservation's value, position and family come from this campaign's own receipts rather than from the source: r = 2 of ten is the smallest integer that guarantees a purchase in all 435 batches, where the Parent bought none in 292 of them; the restricted mask is the same eligibility interface n-61b9b3bfb40d already moved on this ancestry; the family tag already exists on every pool row; and recomputing this exact rule on the Parent's own 435 pools and sampled function values predicts the reserved picks' pricing in advance (mean percentile 0.326 to 0.526, uncertainty percentile 0.602 to 0.822) and shows the empty-mask fallback cannot fire, since every pool held at least 31 prior-origin members.

arxiv.org/html/2402.05961 appendix ablations: default number of GA generations, offspring size, KL coefficient, training loops, and any statement of the per-round policy-versus-GA evaluation split

sources.applicability: The borrowed element is the allocation pattern, not the policy: a fixed per-round integer number of evaluations is committed to learned-generator candidates instead of being competed for against genetic offspring under one score. That is exactly the untested candidate class this Parent's measured refusal calls for, and it is adopted at the one place this arm may change - the allocator's availability mask - while the Parent's own prior, prefix rule, share, temperature and checkpoint stay frozen.
sources.finding: Read Algorithm 1 and the appendix. The method does not let one ranker arbitrate its two proposal origins: each outer iteration scores one molecule sampled from the learned SMILES policy and then scores numGen generations of crossover/mutation offspring, so a fixed integer number of oracle calls per round is spent on learned-generator samples and the rest on genetic offspring. The text does not state numGen numerically; the ablation table for the number of GA generations has its x2 column equal to the headline AUC Top-10 of 16.213 and the offspring-size table has its size-8 column equal to the same value, which indicates the defaults. Population size and replay batch are 64 'the same as the batch size without tuning', mutation rate 0.01, eight training loops, and the benchmark budget is 10,000 oracle calls.
sources.title: Genetic-guided GFlowNets for Sample Efficient Molecular Optimization (NeurIPS 2024)

hypothesis: Inside the inherited correlated Thompson allocation over the mixed-origin 160-member pool, reserve a fixed integer r = 2 of the ten sequential picks for the prior-origin proposal family. The joint posterior draw is unchanged: one (10 x 160) matrix of standard normals is still drawn once per batch from the same generator in the same order and mapped through the same Cholesky factor of the same conditional covariance, so the sampled function values at every position are the values the Parent's rule would have used. Picks at positions 0 through 7 are the inherited rule exactly - the argmax of that position's sampled function over all not-yet-selected pool members, with the inherited first-index tie rule. At positions 8 and 9 the availability mask is additionally restricted to pool members whose recorded origin is prior_continuation and which are not yet selected, and the pick is the argmax of the same position's same sampled function inside that restricted mask. Nothing is re-drawn, re-fitted or re-normalized, and no quantity outside the mask changes. If a reserved position finds no unselected prior-origin member the inherited unrestricted mask is used for that pick and the event is logged; on the Parent's own receipts every one of the 435 pools held at least 31 prior-origin members, so this fallback is expected to be empty. The reservation is one bound integer applied identically in every announced batch of every session: no per-task value, no mid-run adaptation, no schedule, no dependence on score level, task identity or stall state. The causal claim is that this restriction diverts 20% of the evaluation budget to candidates the archive-anchored similarity kernel prices below the incumbent's neighbourhood, and that those forced purchases - not more supply of them - are what determines whether the refusal measured in round 42 was costing realized endpoint gain.

finding_summary.headline: Forced purchase of the declined chemistry activated exactly and was repaid by one cell of fifteen: the pricing hypothesis fails
finding_summary.insights:
The campaign now has the discriminating answer its two round-42 structural-limitation lessons asked for, and it is negative: on this Parent, at 300 evaluations per task, the archive-anchored posterior's refusal to buy prior-origin chemistry was mostly correct pricing, not foregone gain. Forcing 20% of the budget onto that chemistry bought candidates that beat their breeding parents at two thirds the rate, survived at six tenths the rate and improved the incumbent at half the rate of what they displaced, and the reserved fifth of the budget returned less than a fifth of the realized gain in eleven of fifteen sessions. The one session that paid, paid 0.30 of score through a single step event the surrogate under-predicted by 0.27 at a posterior SD of 0.013. That is the real shape of the loss surface here: the benefit of distant chemistry on this benchmark is not a density the allocator can harvest at the margin, it is a rare step whose expected value fifteen sessions cannot estimate. The cheapest member of the reserved-evaluation class is therefore closed with receipts rather than left as an untested prescription, and no share, temperature, prefix, width, depth, checkpoint or quota sweep follows from it.

The method diagnosis is that the limitation is the surrogate's scale, not its ranking, and a reservation cannot reach it. Within batches the Gaussian process ranks well - mean predicted-versus-realized rank correlation 0.608 here against the Parent's 0.534 - but its posterior SD around the incumbent neighbourhood is of order 0.013 while the only move that mattered was worth 0.27. No acquisition rule reading that posterior can prefer such a candidate, and a family reservation does not help, because the family label says nothing about which member is informative: the reserved pick is still the mis-scaled posterior's own argmax inside the family, at in-pool percentile 0.49. What would address it is a different kind of model, not a different quota - a predictor whose uncertainty is comparable across chemotypes (ensemble, deep-kernel or conformally calibrated) or a comparison-trained ranker, combined with an acquisition that prices information rather than score. The companion arms in this round are now the informative contrast: the distance-reserved arm on the Anchor uses the same reserved-mask interface but labels by archive distance instead of proposal family, which separates 'reservation fails' from 'this label fails', and the field-reduction control separates pool composition from allocation.

The trajectories also show a second, separable limitation that no reservation touches. In the one session that found the rewarded scaffold, the remaining 100 evaluations were spent relabelling it: 32 scored at or above 0.90, 8 at exactly 0.905207, median similarity to the conditioning parent 0.887, total further gain +0.006984. The molecular report reads the same way from the chemistry side - narrow structural diversity, one scaffold family in the deco_hop top thirty, every molecule above 0.90 a one-atom decoration of a single parent, saturated amine centres reachable only where the seed population already had a nitrogen, no declared stereochemistry anywhere, and sub-molecular one- and two-atom strings still consuming evaluations. That pattern argues for a fragment-attachment proposal operator and a diversity-aware batch rule (clustered or determinantal selection instead of ten sequential Thompson argmaxes over one pool) plus a minimum-size admission floor, which are proposal- and selection-scheme changes rather than parameter values.

Two narrower things are now settled. First, the deco_hop lesson needs updating: this is the first of thirty-one complete ungated children to satisfy the deco_hop margin against the Anchor (+0.007109, where the previous thirty all fell between -0.116414 and -0.084946), and it did so without reproducing the Anchor's seed-0 0.856148 cell (it scored 0.612855 there) by reaching 0.912192 in a different seed through a different chemistry. The high deco_hop region is reachable by more than one route; it is a step the search hits rarely, not a property of one inherited realization. Second, sitagliptin_mpo's breach is now persistent and deeper (-0.196411 against the Anchor, -0.229935 against the ungated reference), and by this route's own registered condition that ends the route rather than inviting a re-threshold. What stays open: whether reserved allocation fails for the family label or in general, which only the distance-labelled arm can say; and whether a calibrated-uncertainty surrogate would price the step chemistry high enough to buy it without a quota at all.
finding_summary.results:
The reservation activated exactly as registered. All 870 reserved picks (positions nine and ten of 435 announced batches, 15 sessions) bought a prior-origin candidate, with zero empty-mask fallbacks, restricted masks of 28 to 40 members, and 812 of the 870 picks (93.3%) landing on a different candidate from the one the inherited unrestricted draw would have taken at that same position. The prior-origin share of evaluations rose from the Parent's 231 of 4,350 (5.31%) to 1,097 of 4,350 (25.22%), at or above 20% in all 15 sessions, and no announced batch bought none, against the Parent's 292 of 435 empty batches including all 29 batches of sitagliptin seed 2. The diversion was real and not a relabelling: reserved picks sat at in-pool predicted-score percentile 0.490 and uncertainty percentile 0.654, against 0.838 and 0.361 for the eight free picks, which themselves stayed at the Parent's level (0.841 / 0.336) and never deviated from the inherited argmax in any of 3,480 picks; one ten-by-one-hundred-sixty normal draw per batch in 435 of 435 batches, no posterior fallback, and batch-one selections identical to the Parent through the eighth pick in 15 of 15 sessions. The supply was held fixed to the receipt: pooled prior-origin share 0.2487 against the Parent's 0.2486, pools complete at 160 in 435 of 435 batches, the prior's weights byte-identical to the Parent's for every seed with zero online updates, no oracle labels and no stored corpus molecules.

Conversion is where the hypothesis died. The prior-origin group's share of realized incumbent-increment mass rose from 2.79% to 20.51% (1.1114 of 5.4187 against the Parent's 0.1405 of 5.0403), but that share reached its own 20-25% evaluation share in only 3 of 15 sessions, against the registered six, and the reserved positions returned 0.9784 of the node's 5.4187 total mass - 18.1% of the gain for 20% of the budget. Per evaluation the forced purchases were plainly worse than what they displaced: parent-beat rate 0.099 against 0.155, survivor admission 0.498 against 0.832, incumbent-improvement rate 0.030 against 0.059, and a more negative mean child-minus-best-parent in 14 of the 15 sessions. In one realization the prior-origin increment mass gained 0.9709 while the graph-origin mass lost 0.5925. The registered recovery prediction failed outright: sitagliptin_mpo, named in advance as the task with a measured mechanism to recover, lost 0.0625 against the Parent and 0.1964 against the Anchor, and its seed-2 session - the one that had bought nothing in 29 batches - bought 63 prior candidates, beat a breeding parent once in 63, improved the incumbent zero times, returned 0.0000 increment mass, and the cell fell 0.1173.

The paired fifteen-cell panel against the code Parent is +0.025228 (0.569740 against 0.544512; seeds -0.021619, +0.052101, +0.045204; 10 of 15 cells positive), and 79.0% of it is a single cell: deco_hop seed 2 at +0.298890. Drop that one cell and the panel mean is +0.005302, inside the ungated law-free reference band's half-width of 0.040983, which is the registered opposite-way refutation. Against the Anchor the node is -0.026713, inside the ungated band; its must-preserve task means are deco_hop +0.007109 (margin 0.02), drd2_docking -0.007518 (0.03), zaleplon_mpo +0.036142 (0.02), median_2 +0.027114 with cells 0.258268 / 0.236775 / 0.254494, and sitagliptin_mpo -0.196411, a deepened breach of its 0.02 margin against the Parent's own -0.133933.

The deco_hop seed-2 cell resolves to one purchase. At batch 19 the reserved position nine bought a prior continuation scoring 0.905207 and carrying an incumbent increment of +0.242796 - 66.7% of that session's whole 0.363810 gain and 64.2% of the entire fifteen-cell panel movement. It is the prior's half-prefix continuation of a scored 0.659675 parent, which rebuilt the 6,7-dimethoxy-4-anilinoquinazoline with a methylenedioxy aniline. But at that position the inherited unrestricted rule would have bought exactly the same pool member: it is one of the 58 of 870 reserved picks the restriction did not change, so the decisive purchase is not attributable to the reservation. What the reservation did buy is the road to it: the conditioning parent's own ancestry runs through reserved picks at batches 1, 2 (both, whose crossover first displayed the anilino-methylenedioxy motif), 5, 11 and 17, eight of those ten being genuine diversions, and the Parent's own deco_hop seed 2 never entered that chemistry at all - 7 of its 290 molecules carried a methylenedioxy fragment, best score 0.598480, and it plateaued at 0.613301 on an unrelated triazolylpyridine series. The event is also unrepeated: it happened once in fifteen sessions, the surrogate predicted 0.63422 for it at a posterior SD of 0.01308 (a 20-sigma miss), and the 100 evaluations that followed it in that session returned a further +0.006984 in total.

molecular.headline: Flat polymethoxy/aminoquinazoline/benzodioxole aromatics with 3-5 rings, no declared stereochemistry, and recurring N-F, peroxide and one-atom proposals.
molecular.overall_character: Across all five objectives the node proposed 870 molecules each (290 per seed, three seeds) and the sets are chemically of one kind: heavily ring-fused, almost entirely aromatic flat scaffolds of 24-30 heavy atoms and MW 344-431, decorated by single-atom edits. The string counters agree with that reading - ring_closure_rate 0.9747-0.9874 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9621-0.9805 on every set - so ring and aromatic content is genuinely rich, not sparse. What the sets lack is everything orthogonal to that manifold: stereocentre_rate is 0.0 in all five sets even though the majority of molecules on three of them carry an undefined tetrahedral centre, median fsp3 is 0.18-0.42, saturated and bridged carbocycles are almost never built, and saturated amine rings appear only where the incumbent already had a nitrogen to edit. The two registers the generator draws from are visibly different chemistry: the local-edit products are larger, more halogenated and harder to make (median SA 2.96-5.16, halogen in up to 94.7%), while the corpus-prior continuations are smaller and cleaner (median SA 2.56-3.88, fewer thiols, almost no N-halogen bonds). The honest liability across every set is admission hygiene rather than ambition: N-fluoroanilines, aryl peroxides, N-F and N-SH ring substituents, chloromethyl ethers, arene-fused four-membered oxygen rings, aziridines and N,O-aminals all survive to be scored, and so do single- and two-atom strings such as C, Cl, FF, OS and NNS.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: Two things move the score: adding fluorine to one sp3 carbon until it is CF2 or CF3, and closing another ring to make the skeleton more compact and more fused. Halogen presence goes from 33% in the bottom 100 to 100% in the top 30 and CF2/CF3 from 8% to 86.7%, while synthetic accessibility gets worse monotonically (median SA 4.05 in the bottom 100, 5.75 in the top 30). The objective is clearly rewarding the fluorine count and a specific heavy-atom/ring profile, and the generator pays for that in ring strain.

transferable_gaps.evidence: N-fluoroaniline nitrogen appears in 16.7% of one set's top 30 (CN(F) on a benzylamine) and as n(F) and n2S ring substituents in the best and final molecules of another; an aryl peroxide COO sits in the single highest-scoring molecule of a third set, alongside O[O-], OCCl chloromethyl ether, and N-O/N-N linkers such as CSN1OCN. Acyclic N-N string patterns run at 12.5% of one whole set.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits heteroatom-heteroatom and nitrogen-halogen bonds as ordinary decorations, so a measurable share of its highest-scoring molecules are not real compounds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The admission path accepts any valence-legal graph, so the sanity of a bond pair is never checked. A task-blind rejection list over N-halogen, N-S, N-O, O-O and O-halogen bonds outside nitro/sulfonyl/sulfonamide contexts would remove these without any knowledge of what is being optimized, and the top molecules of the sets where that chemistry is absent show the search does not need it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The SMILES-level stereocentre_rate is 0.0 in all five sets, while RDKit finds an undefined tetrahedral centre in 83.3%, 67.1% and 32.3% of three of them; the highest-scoring molecules of two sets are fused bicyclics whose ring-fusion carbons are centres with no configuration written.
transferable_gaps.gap: No proposal declares stereochemistry, although most of them contain stereocentres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Neither the local-edit operators nor the crossover ever write or carry a configuration tag, so every candidate is a configurationally averaged string and an objective that distinguishes enantiomers cannot be climbed. An operator set that assigns configuration at a centre it creates and preserves the parent's tags through edits would make the proposals single molecules.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Scored proposals include the one- and two-atom strings C, Cl, FF, OS, NNS, C#C, CC, OCCl and F, appearing in the worst-molecule sets of three of the five objectives and scoring zero in every case.
transferable_gaps.gap: Candidate size has no lower floor, so the generator proposes and spends evaluations on sub-molecular fragments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The delete-atom and open-ring operators can walk a 25-atom candidate down to a single atom with no heavy-atom, ring-count or connectivity floor at emission, and a fixed evaluation budget pays for each one. A minimum heavy-atom and minimum ring-count check at proposal time is objective-blind and recovers those evaluations outright.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Basic amine presence across the five sets ranges from 5.3% and 7.1% to 88.7%, and the two sets at the bottom have zero basic amines in their top 30 while the three above have 76.7% to 100%; piperazine presence is 0.0-9.4% overall and 43.3% in exactly one top 30, the one whose seed molecules already carried a piperazine.
transferable_gaps.gap: Saturated nitrogen heterocycles are only reached by editing a nitrogen the incumbent already has, never attached as a unit, so basic amine centres are near-absent wherever the starting population lacked them.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The operator family is atom- and bond-local plus a scaffold-level crossover, with no fragment-attachment move, so a saturated amine ring can only emerge from a lucky sequence of single edits. A fragment-level attachment operator carrying a small library of saturated heterocycles would make that centre reachable from any starting population.

transferable_gaps.evidence: aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9621-0.9805 over all 4,350 proposals and ring_closure_rate 0.9747-0.9874, while median fsp3 stays at 0.18-0.42 with four of the five sets at or below 0.31; where an objective visibly rewarded a compact non-aromatic skeleton, the generator reached it by fusing more rings onto an already aromatic core and median synthetic accessibility rose to 5.75 in that top 30.
transferable_gaps.gap: Almost every ring the generator adds is aromatic, so it cannot move a population off the flat aromatic manifold into saturated or bridged aliphatic space.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The ring-closing operator acts in whatever hybridization context it finds, which is overwhelmingly aromatic, and there is no move that produces a saturated or bridged ring as such. A ring-forming operator that constructs saturated and bridged rings, and a crossover that can exchange an aliphatic framework, would open that region of chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Arene-fused four-membered oxygen rings (the c3O4 and c3CO4 patterns) appear in a majority of the molecules that reached the maximum score on one objective; aziridine N1CC1 appears in two of the twelve best molecules of another and 1,3-diazetidine/aminal N1CNC1 in the best and final molecules of a third.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring closures default to the smallest ring geometrically available, so strained three- and four-membered rings accumulate in exactly the molecules the search is rewarding.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Nothing in the ring-closure move weights the resulting ring size, so the cheapest closure is the most strained one and it is then conserved by selection. Weighting closures by resulting ring size, or rejecting fused three- and four-membered carbo/heterocycles outside recognized contexts, is objective-blind and leaves the rest of the search untouched.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Comparing the two tagged proposal families within each of the five sets, the corpus-prior continuations run at median SA 2.56-3.88 against 2.96-5.16 for the local-edit products, with lower halogen rates and almost no thiols or N-halogen bonds; yet they hold only 0, 1, 1, 3 and 9 of the thirty top positions in the five sets. On one objective the entire high-scoring region descends from a single prior-origin molecule whose scaffold the other two seeds never produced.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has two chemically distinct registers, and the cleaner one produces molecules that are smaller, less halogenated and easier to make but is never refined by the local-edit arm.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Describing this as chemistry, not attribution: the two registers do not compose, because a continuation product is not available as a breeding parent for the local-edit arm until it has been evaluated, and its scaffold is therefore never decorated unless it happens to be bought. A generator that let the distant-chemistry register seed the local-edit register directly would combine clean scaffolds with the decoration the local edits are good at.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
